name: Black Ghost
imitates: A classic eastern feather-wing baitfish streamer, slim and flashy, for trout and landlocked salmon in rivers and lakes.
recipe: Four white Chinese rooster neck hackles

steps.text: Wrap a thread base to the bend and tie in a clump of yellow hen fibers as the tail, extending about one gap width past the bend.
Tie in a second clump of hen fibers as an underbody to even out the shank, and smooth it with thread. Tie in the tinsel underneath.
Wrap the black floss in several smooth, tight layers up and back to build a slightly tapered body.
Re-start the black thread at the front of the body and spiral the flat tinsel forward in six to eight tight, even turns. Tie off and smooth a thread base to the eye.
Invert the hook and tie in a clump of yellow hen fibers as a beard that reaches to the middle of the shank. Trim the butts at an angle and turn the hook back up.
Match four white rooster hackles in two pairs, inside to inside, and bind them on top of the shank at the front of the body in a narrow band.
Trim the quill stubs, then tie in a matched jungle cock nail on each side of the wing at the same angle.
Trim the butts, build a smooth tapered head and whip finish. Add two coats of head lacquer.
Finished Black Ghost: black floss body with silver rib, yellow tail and beard, white wing and jungle cock eyes.
